'''''Phagnalon rupestre''''', '''rock phagnalon''', is a species of shrub in the family [[Asteraceae]]. It is native to the Mediterranean basin countries of Europe, North Africa, and Western Asia, and to Iran, Iraq, the Arabian Peninsula, and the Canary Islands.<ref name = powo/>

They have a self-supporting growth form, simple, broad leaves and dry fruit. Individuals can grow to 0.25 m.<ref>{{Cite web|title=''Phagnalon rupestre'' (L.) DC. - Encyclopedia of Life|url=https://eol.org/pages/6275144|access-date=2022-02-04|website=eol.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mifsud |first=Stephen |date=2002-08-23 |title=Phagnalon rupestre subsp. graecum (Eastern Phagnalon) : MaltaWildPlants.com - the online Flora of the Maltese Islands. |url=https://www.maltawildplants.com/ASTR/Phagnalon_rupestre_subsp_graecum.php |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=www.maltawildplants.com |language=en-us}}</ref>

Two subspecies are accepted.<ref name = powo/>
*''Phagnalon rupestre'' subsp. ''morisianum'' {{small|(Ces., Pass. & Gibelli) Arcang.}} – Sardinia
*''Phagnalon rupestre'' subsp. ''rupestre'' – entire range
